subject: A Small Bit to Add
author: Abernyte
body:
I am on a year and three months of playing BP and it remains the game I am most likely to pop into the PS3. That said, I really see so much more potential to this game. You've covered most things that I find bother me so rather than reiterate I'll just emphasize a few of your points:

Splashes: these need to move out of the main field of view or have an on/off switch. All of the information displayed on the screen needs to be reduced, or at least be user selectable.

Racing: I don't race in this game but I completely understand the frustration of racers. CG needs to do something to address the frustration of these folks as they represent an important part of their customer base. I'd even give racing another go if they intriduced blind matchmaking and random races. I'd probably still lose but I'd give it a shot.

Takedowns: I don't know how, but these need to be fixed. If it isn't technically possible to properly sync people's systems so that both see the same data and can therefore predict when and how takedowns will occur, then make it harder to take people down, or reduce the number of second that you loose control. I hope to never again here the phrase "Who the hell did I take down? There's nobody near me."

Fog: What can I say but get rid of it, or at least put in an on/off switch. I can put up with takedown jockeys in challenges, magically appearing traffic, wrecking on invisible object etc. Fog is one of th few things that will get me to simply turn off the game and walk away. From a technical standpoint the introduction of the fog to the environent is impressive. But it simple adds nothing positive to the game experience.

Cars/Colors/Customization: I don't need to tweak the suspension on every car, but I would like to make my cars a bit unique. The popularity of the color glitch indicates that many others do as well. Give me fewer cars (many of which most people never use) with more flexibility to control their appearance. I'd also like a favorites menu; I don't need to scroll through 100 cars to find the five I actually drive regularly.

BSI: I was incredibly excited about BSI. The potential I saw when I played the beta version back in September was huge! After having played on it for a few days I found myself back in the Airfield last night. BSI is incredible for what it is. But it's dissapointing for what it's not. What I was expecting and hoping for was a location where we could get bigger spins, more rolls, etc. What I've seen so far is lots of locations for stunts but nothing that beats what we had in the old city. It's a matter of quantity vs. quality. Most of the jumps are heavily limited by the run ups. For example compare the top of the Quarry to the split ramps on the top of the construction site on BSI. What really kills me is the two biggest jumps on BSI, the bridge and ski jumps, lack split ramps or anything to clip for spins. They are great jumps for air times and jump distances but I think they missed the mark.

I'm sure the telemetry they received showed a ton of people in the Airfield and at the Dam/Quarry area. What it apparently didn't show them is what they were actually doing in those areas. Not just jumps but spins and rolls.

Sadly the "if you see it you can drive it" tag line is less than accurate. I absolutely understand that you can't have a game without wreck zones. But there are so many areas that you can easily jump to that are wreck zones. The construction site is a great example. You can readily get onto many of the under construction floors but they are wreck zones.

The "new" cars were also disappointing to me. I now have two versions of three cars I'll never drive, the Olympus, the Spirit and the bootlegger. I do like the toy 88 special, the toy nighthawk and the two dust storms. Not sure on the street rod. Have to say that the diamond P12 was a disappointment. I actually completed 490 challenges for four separate IDs, partly for something to do, partly in anticipation of the rumoured prize. I love the P12 and it is my car of choice for challenges. I was hoping for a variation on it, say a carbon. What I got was improved stats and a paint job that will keep me from driving the thing. My tastes run to the more subtle. Could I just get a stripe that has the number 500 integrated into it?

Marketing/Public Relations: It seems as though CG has never quite gotten the hang of interacting with the hard core fans. Clearly their overall approach has worked given how many copies of the game they sold. But they never seemed to know how do deal with the criticism they received on the old forums and their reaction to it was handled poorly. If you invite comment you need to be prepared to receive it. When you make a mistake, admit it. In fairness, as one of the "Rai-Jin beta testers", as well as someone who put a fair amount of effort into the old CG forums, I'm still a bit bitter about how that all played out so my opinion in that regard should be considered with that in mind. Further, I fully recognize that many of the fans contributed heavily to that entire situation; CG is not solely to blame.

Overall: This is, without a question, my favorite game. Incredible graphics, terrific sense of speed and the best online experience of any game I've payed. I have spent a ridiculous amount of time playing it, taken days off from work for updates, made friends across the world (some of whom I've met in person), and generally been obsessed with it. It is, simply put, a phenominal game. But it can be much more. We'll see what the future brings.

Hhhmmm, perhaps "a samll bit to add" wasn't the most appropriate title!

subject: Expectations, hopes and dreams...
author: ZombieTron
body:
I was in an enviable position of playing Paradise at Criterion Games studios for a weekend back in October 2007, feels like a lifetime ago now! So, I got a feel of what Paradise was a few months before release.  I pretty much spent the weekend in a whirl as it was a very exciting experience and Paradise was very different to the other Burnouts and I couldn't really take it all in. 

When January rolled around I was still shocked that there was no online Road Rage?? I figured this would be a given and that we just weren't shown this when we visited as we were just shown the new stuff.

There were lots of things that have been added in DLC which I think should have been in the game from day 1. This is what gives me the most negative feelings about Paradise.

I found it very odd that there was not more to do online when the game first came out. Online Stunt Run, Road Rage and Marked Man were all added fairly quickly, but not quickly enough for a lot of the original Burners to keep with the game.

Another initial mistake was the VOIP problems on the 360... joining random rooms and not being able to communicate really killed the game for me as I was not able to feel like part of the community.

I think Paradise has suffered from lots of little hic-cups like this.

When we spoke to CG about the checkpoints early on, they didn't want visual checkpoints as it made it look too gamey, they wanted to create a submersive environment, what was the word they used all the time at the beginning? Seamless! Give you a world and not put anything in it which will take you out of that world.

I think the visual checkpoints they have added to the Island are among the best visual checkpoints of any racing game I have seen. These for me would have made a HUGE impact to my enjoyment of racing in Paradise if they had of been included from the beginning, even adding them now as the checkpoints we can use for online racing will improve the game 100% for us racers.

Visual checkpoints mean you can look at the road, focus on the race, and not just watch the mini-map to make sure you are going the right way.

Having a rotating mini-map, or the option to pick what kind of mini-map you want would have been great too.

On the Big Surf Island Q&A on Totally 360.com Pete Lake is asked "Will there be any gameplay updates with this DLC? Such as the ability to place waypoints on the map to allow players to converge on an area more easily?"

What a great idea! This also leads to being able to set up our own online challenges. I know we can sort of do this anyway... in the same way that we can race on bikes just by saying to each other start at Wildcats and end up at the Windfarm.. but having it actually in the game engine seems so obvious I don't know why it wasn't included.

Thanks for the Blog Suf! and for inviting me to spew my 2 cents... I was hoping for a better racing experience, and when that was lacking a more rounded polished vision instead of the sandbox do it your way game which I struggle with. I need a bit more direction. 🙂

author: SUFFUR
body:
...watch the community made videos, from Youtube or in the community site links.

So they knew what were were doing! I assume? They must know right?

I think the community took the game way beyond thier expectations, but maybe they could also think we were abusing what they have made, smashing into the side of the Dam and pushing the car spin physics or a-watcha-ma-call-it's-I-don't-know-what-but-i'll-pretend-you-do-even-if-i-fake-it-for-ya-type-of-thing, lol, to new hieghts or spins, lol, and bugger up the way you were expected to play, maybe?

What do I know, I'm Hard core fan or hard Core fan, a fan of cores that are hard, anyway, or am I?

But I do know that Revenge and Burnout 3, well the rest of the games really, got my heart pumping, hands sweating, and my adrenaline going, to the point I feared for my health for the first time in ages today, though I had sort of calmed down by the time I was invited to fill up a room in the Revenge Tourney, which I wanted to do, but was not really prepared for, but had fun, knowing I was almost as good as the winners, a few years ago now, and got throughly owned, but I digress once again, thats for another blog, at another time in the future.

 

There's lots of free-burn videos, stunt runs and hidding spot and pictures of great spin and rolls.

There are not many videos of racing, because not many people are doing it, as it is faulty, defunct, and just ssessip people off.

I enjoyed hn6's Road Rule videos, but how many 'takes' did he have to go throught to show some damn find speeding!

The main game was not really designed to race in, it can be, but the Island was so right, it worked in Single player really well, a lot of the others on the main land do too.

The Island's Check points and routes were well balanced, with alternate routes but still near competators, the corners were cuttable, and some sweet driving, drifting and jumping oppertunities, true it is a bit small, but the online would have lasted a bit longer after running different variations of routes, cars, time of day etc.

But stunt run wise the Island is choc-full of stunt run points, high scoring is easy, but some have got used to the Extreme Hot Rod to do stunt runs, at high speed and that is really hard to do in the confines that have been set up with some wreak zones, jump placements and inclines, as well as air space between the jumps. If the quarry was just a deep curved basin, with lots of in and outs and no objects in the way but split ramps and drops, it would be a stunt runners play ground for the big hitters.

I like stunt running on the Island but I normally run it in the Roadster that had a good pace to it, but has got slower with this update, so getting use to the Toy P12 88 Special, for it's air and spins, though it's a bugger when it hits a wall, it's so slow to reverse out of those situations, which kills a combo, quick if your not careful.

Anyway Criterion did a good play ground, it just not extreme mad elite enough is all, lol.

But still early days, someone may find a great spot, I know Kev and I have had fun looking.

Patience is something I taught myself, so I never know when it's going to run out?

 

I also though more people would have something to say on this tread, which can mean a few things, their still playing it, and love it which is good, moved on which is bad, sad but understandable, or no-one cares or is bothered, lol, for the Island or maybe even my views, but either way, no worries, mate!

But do say something, I am interested, I'm a lonely, sad man, that needs this, really I am, I have a cause, to find a great arcade racer, with amazing stuff going on it, that brings us all together again, including my new friends from Paradise, and we are all joined together in a hug of love and freindship and caring, really I want this, then it will spread across the universe, and we will all die happy and content.
